migration.migration_reason: Preserved paid Language Quality findings were independently re-adjudicated against the current fixed five-component design rubric. Legacy normalized scores were retained only for audit and were not used to derive component levels. The snapshot is bound to exact source evidence and the current validator recomputes scores.

recertifier.provider_model_provenance_claim: No Anthropic/Sonnet call is claimed for these reconstructed judgments.

component_findings.actionability: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Messages normally provide enough precise information to correct the issue without requiring unrelated guesswork; suggested fixes count only when semantically reliable. Evidence basis: Compiled a representative program derived from ADV-01_C.zig with zig 0.16.0 build/run and captured raw compiler diagnostics. | Compile-time diagnostics for @intCast catch narrowing/overflow at compile time for comptime-known values, with precise file:line:column, a caret-annotated excerpt, and message naming both the offending value and target type. | Error output includes a 'referenced by' inlining/call trace aiding localization through generic/inlined call chains. | Runtime safety builds (Debug/ReleaseSafe) produce panics with backtrace and source location for detectable UB (integer overflow, bounds, null unwrap), relevant to the ADV-01..ADV-26 adversarial UB corpus. | Weaknesses: comptime error chains can cascade/verbose for generic instantiation failures; evolving stdlib API surface (e.g. std.Io.Threaded, std.process.Init.Minimal) across compiler versions produces version-specific diagnostic noise. | zig run test1.zig | test1.zig:10:29: error: type 'i32' cannot represent integer value '9223372036854775807' const b: i32 = @intCast(a); referenced-by trace through std.start callMain/callMainWithArgs/posixCallMainAndExit | 0-100, 100 = best diagnostics | zig 0.16.0

metric.diagnostics.limitations: Comparison-language reprojection requires the preserved paid source evidence plus the historical program/workload/toolchain inputs to match the current shard; mismatches remain misses.
metric.diagnostics.selection_rule: Judge built-in compiler/checker/runtime diagnostic design from normal language use; do not count external IDE/debugger maturity.

component_findings.abstraction_reuse: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Functions, modules/types and generic/polymorphic abstraction support reusable composition across ordinary programs. Evidence basis: Inspection of assigned Zig adversarial (ADV-01..26) and micro (mb00..mb11) programs under /quidra-benchmark/template/programs/zig, plus compiler probes with zig 0.16.0. | Zig uses comptime generics (comptime parameters, anytype) instead of traits/interfaces; no operator overloading; no exceptions -- error unions with try/catch give explicit but verbose control flow for generic abstraction relative to Rust traits or Kotlin/Swift protocols. | No stable first-class async/await in this build; micro workloads use std.Io.Threaded abstraction instead, reducing concurrency expressiveness relative to Go goroutines or async/await languages. | Comptime metaprogramming allows generic containers/algorithms without runtime cost, a distinctive expressiveness strength observed across micro workloads. | Manual allocator-passing memory management gives fine control but is more verbose than GC languages for common data structure workloads. | Switch expressions and error unions provide reasonable but not maximal expressiveness compared to pattern matching in Rust/Kotlin. | 0-100, 100 = most expressive
